title: Kept methods with other parameters are called as their old selves behaved
text: The biggest type of break, call, game: linked (a game method still there with other parameters), is handled as a type: each parameter of the new method is read from where the old and new bodies line up. Where the new body uses a parameter, the old body's value there is what to pass: an old operand, a fixed value, a fixed value solved through a sum (1.21.2's sea level: seaLevel + 17 where the old body had 80), a value of the receiver (this.level(), narrowed to ServerLevel), or the value a callee that changed the same way needs. A value of another type is made with the new type's constructor or its one static factory; a parameter the new body never reads takes its type's zero, only for methods nothing overrides.
finish: the type's finishes and mods counts down across every update (tools/cloud-run exposure, types in all.json), port.jar-links.newest and big-updates no lower, and load on a real server for the updates it frees most
wrongIf: a mod that links through a learned argument behaves differently in game from its old version
result: 2026-11-21: call, game: linked over every update finishes 186 -> 177 and is in 1,984 -> 1,960 mods (2,965 -> 2,877 references). Every update 5,884 -> 5,893 of 9,423, none lower; big updates 1,896 -> 1,904; newest jump 15 -> 15; jumps 1,167 -> 1,173. NeoForge 1.21.1 -> 1.21.2 40 -> 42 (the Biome family takes the old sea level, 63): on a real 1.21.2 server 22 of 25 linked mods load (main 21 of 24), in the client 23 of 23; Coroutil, newly linked, loads in both. Not handled: parameters whose value the old body never had (CycleButton.builder's initial value, 1.21.9's permission levels), redesigned types (TicksToSave -> PackedTicks, String -> ResourceKey), and methods an override may change. 2026-11-23: reshaped constructors are called so the object they build holds what the old one did: both constructors are run over their parameters as sums, each field the old one set is read as the learner says the new release reads it, and each new parameter is solved (1.20.3's selection lists: height = y1 - y0); port rules may add and subtract whole numbers; an argument is left out only where the old game never used what it set; a constructor no longer links through a superclass's with the same parameters. The type finishes 97 -> 81 and is in 1,551 -> 1,530 mods; every update 6,596 -> 6,610, big updates 2,438 -> 2,451, newest 22 -> 22; Fabric 1.20.2 -> 1.20.3 96 -> 106, NeoForge 107 -> 113; four false links caught (old constructors that linked through a super's: ServerCore, Totally Lit, Forge Config API Port, Make Bubbles Pop). In a real 1.20.3 client 7 of 10 freed Fabric mods load and 6 of 7 NeoForge, every server one on a server; the three that fail do so outside this change (a gone mixin point, pack loading, reflection by intermediary name). Not handled: a parameter whose value lives in a type the new release builds otherwise (1.17's EntityRendererProvider.Context, 1.20's GuiGraphics), and methods an override may change.
